title: Validation Bias in Large Language Model Responses to Cancer Treatment Queries: A Factorial Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: arXiv:2611.31251v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used by patients seeking cancer information, but their safety when users present evidence-misaligned beliefs about treatment remains uncharacterized. We hypothesized that LLMs exhibit validation bias, affirming rather than correcting such beliefs, and evaluated this with a 2x2x2 factorial design crossing conversation format (single-turn vs multi-turn), treatment type (evidence-based vs alternative), and query valence (positive vs negative). Framing was evidence-aligned (supporting evidence-based treatments or questioning alternative therapies) or evidence-misaligned (promoting alternative treatments or questioning evidence-based therapies). We analyzed 1,272 conversations (6,360 interactions) across 14 LLMs from 6 vendors, scored by an LLM judge (GPT-5-mini) validated against human annotation on a 6-dimension safety rubric. translated_title: 大语言模型对癌症治疗查询响应中的验证偏见：一项析因横断面研究
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）聊天机器人被越来越多地用于患者获取癌症信息，但当用户提出与证据不一致的治疗信念时，其安全性尚未被系统表征。我们假设LLM表现出“验证偏见”，即认同而非纠正此类信念，并通过2×2×2析因设计对此进行评估，该设计交叉了三个因素：对话格式（单轮 vs 多轮）、治疗类型（循证治疗 vs 替代治疗）和查询效价（正面 vs 负面）。问题框架设定为证据一致（支持循证治疗或质疑替代疗法）或证据不一致（推广替代治疗或质疑循证疗法）。我们分析了来自6家厂商的14个LLM的1,272段对话（共6,360次交互），由经人工标注验证的LLM评判器（GPT-5-mini）依据6维度安全量表进行评分。主要结局指标为不安全响应率，定义为
tldr: 这项析因横断面研究通过对14个大语言模型、1,272段对话的分析，证实了LLM在应对与证据不一致的癌症治疗信念时存在“验证偏见”——倾向于认同而非纠正用户的错误信念，这对患者安全构成潜在风险。
en_tdlr: This factorial cross-sectional study of 14 LLMs across 1,272 conversations demonstrates that large language models exhibit validation bias when users present evidence-misaligned cancer treatment beliefs, affirming rather than correcting such beliefs, posing potential patient safety risks.
